Verdicts.Verdict:
Reviewed against the amended spec by the authority. Review 0 findings; WriteEvidence scope audit 45 paths 0 findings; attempt-pair audit 5 pairs 0 findings; scope audit not-run on a clean tree, the honest F27 case. Verified independently from the tree, not from the report: validate:ci exit 0, suite 1344 pass 3 skip 0 fail, and each of the three repaired pins read at its own site.
DISCLOSURE 1, THE LARGEST. THE APPROVED spec.xml AND plan.xml WERE AMENDED IN PLACE, AFTER APPROVAL AND MID-EPOCH. ngrace-plan SKILL.md approved_plan_immutability forbids refreshing ObservedWriteScope in place and directs a superseding bundle. The authority raised that path, priced it, and the user directed the in-place amendment as an explicit exception. This is recorded as a deliberate departure, not reframed as compliance. Cause is F64: the approved write scope missed three CI-load-bearing pins the deliverable inevitably falsifies. That miss is the authority's, caught by the executor, which stopped rather than choosing between a scope breach and a failed task.
DISCLOSURE 2, AND IT LIMITS DISCLOSURE 1. The WriteEvidence audit's 0 findings over 45 paths is not evidence those writes were in scope when they were made. The audit reads the amended plan. Event 21's validate-ci fail carries WriteEvidence that could not name src/grace-cursor.test.ts, scripts/release-check.ts, or scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts, because they were not in ObservedWriteScope when that fail was recorded. So the pin-repair pair has a fail side that cannot name the files that made CI red. The executor identified this as the F9 shape, entered by the authority's missed scope rather than by executor sequencing. After this amendment the two artifacts read as though those four paths were always in scope; only the plan's DESIGN paragraph and this verdict say otherwise.
DISCLOSURE 3. decisions.md was written during the open window. F62.1 and F63 landed before the epoch opened (a723ff3); F64 landed mid-window in its own commit (01695c1), the implementation and the artifact amendment each in their own commits after it. decisions.md is outside every bundle's ObservedWriteScope by design, and the scope audit reads working-tree porcelain, so committing removed it from the audit's view rather than clearing it.
DISCLOSURE 4, A DEFECT THE BUNDLE ALMOST SHIPPED. The first README completeness check was scoped to the whole CLI Overview section, which kept it green under a table-row rename because the Output modes prose also names doctor. That is the same class this bundle exists to retire: a teaching surface a mention elsewhere can keep green. Discrimination caught it — renaming the doctor row to medic, observing the section matcher still pass, tightening to lines beginning with a backtick-ngrace table cell, then observing missing doctor. A clean-tree pass would not have caught it.
DISCLOSURE 5. README and its check were folded into T-005 because T-005 was the open close task, spending its second signature on work that should have been its own task had the artifacts decided README at authoring. The recorded readme-commands fail was against the looser section matcher; the three commands were absent from the table rows too, so the red is the right colour, but table-scoping is proved by the doctor rename, not by that event.
DISCLOSURE 6, DEFERRED WITH THE CONFLICT STATED. The user's standing rule that every phase ships updated docs and examples is enforced by nothing in the product. No requirement in ngrace-spec or ngrace-plan obliges a spec that adds a user-visible command to decide README.md or examples/. This bundle cannot fix that: it forbids SKILL.md edits under F51. Owed to the next bundle.
DISCLOSURE 7. F42 forbade a Target MustContain of the AC-SKELETON needle on skill-contracts.test.ts, since that string is one the teaching emission legitimately carries; the assertion was dropped and the pin itself still asserts it. The three pins were repaired, never weakened: the writer inventory remains a closed set that gained a fifth member and still requires the original four; the packed allowlist gained one path and its test still parses release-check.ts source; the template contract keeps its exact matcher on the id the templates now emit. scripts/release-check.test.ts was verified unnecessary and left out of scope.
DISCLOSURE 8. The executor followed the repository's ngrace-execute SKILL.md over a stale installed copy that drops the same-signature qualifier on the fix budget. The repo copy matches decideFixBudgetEscalation. That installed copy is outside this repository and cannot be fixed here.
